children.text: “我们是密斯卡托尼克大学派来做勘察的。”
“我们是来参加盛宴的。”

引言 1：1926年6月

密斯卡托尼克勘察队，1926年6月。成员：马奎兹、马斯格雷夫等人。

经过密斯卡托尼克大学董事会与拨款委员会的三轮分别审核，我们终于抵达铁杉岛。车夫带我们穿过一道他们称作“堤道”的天然陆桥——只有在退潮时才能通行——来到一个叫阿克望的小渔村。伯蒂向当地人展示了几张那种碱性花朵的素描和照片，可他们全都不买账。也或许是不买他的账。伯蒂倒是兴高采烈得很。

勘察队由我本人、我的助手伯蒂·马斯格雷夫，以及阿米蒂奇博士的几位熟人组成。他坚持要他们陪我来，这是拨款条件的一部分。我只希望他们别碍事。这座岛是私人产业，已经有一段时间禁止访客进入——直到现在。当地人正在整个新英格兰宣传某种节庆，甚至远至南边的波士顿和阿卡姆。

阿克望没有落脚的旅店，而据当地传言，在岛上露营是件危险的事。我再三追问，当地人却闭口不谈，但至少我弄到了一张岛屿地图和一些基本补给。我们几乎已经认命，准备在阿克望西边搭帐篷，这时遇见了一个叫希奥的年轻人，他提出让我们住进一个叫“铁杉谷”的村庄。

罗莎·马奎兹博士

“不过说真的，我觉得你们会喜欢这里的，”希奥从卡车车窗里喊道。马奎兹博士——四十岁，体格健壮，皮肤晒得黝黑——合上勘察日志，抬头望向天空。“我认识的人里，没有一个不喜欢铁杉岛的，”希奥继续说道。“我也不知道我们怎么没早点邀请人来！我猜你们是为盛宴来的吧。”

“这场盛宴是某种当地传统吗？”伯蒂用清脆的英国口音问道。微风拂动这个圆润男子浓密的头发，他热切地向前倾身。

“这是有史以来第一次！山谷里的每个人都使出了浑身解数，好让大家都感到宾至如归。有访客来，我们真是太激动了！”卡车翻过山头时，这个年轻人大笑起来。铁杉岛向四面八方延伸开去。

南面，闪闪发亮的黑色湖泊点缀着杂乱的沼泽，一直延伸到海岸。北面，一座座白顶山丘环绕着突出的黑曜岩，宛如一根裸露的脊骨。越过连绵的山丘，茂密的西部森林顺着多石的山坡向上生长，被一条宽阔的河流一分为二。再往北，越过那些白色的山丘，便是荒凉的多石海岸，紧邻着石板灰的大西洋。

道路带着你们穿过葱郁的农田，驶入一座依偎在山丘间的小村庄。屋顶和栅栏柱上挂着花哨的花饰和鲜艳的缎带。无云的天空中闪耀着一道棱镜般的彩虹，给眼前的景象添上一层田园牧歌的气息。卡车在十字路口停下时，披着白金斗篷、戴着木制动物面具的当地人和孩子围了上来，个个咧着嘴笑。

“欢迎！”一位留着钢灰色头发、身披白金斗篷的威严女子穿过人群。“欢迎来到铁杉谷。我是蕾切尔嬷嬷，这些是我的族人。是什么风把你们吹来的？”

调查员们必须决定（选择一项）：

• “我们是密斯卡托尼克大学派来做勘察的。” 前往 引言 2。

• “我们是来参加盛宴的。” 跳到 引言 3。

引言 2：你报上自己的名字和勘察队成员的名字，并说明你们有密斯卡托尼克大学的支持。马奎兹博士把手杖撑得很重，伸出一只手来与你相握。

• 在本战役余下的时间里，将1枚 [tablet] 标记加入混乱袋。

• 前往 引言 4。

引言 3：女主人慈祥地笑了。“你们能来，我们不胜欢喜。我们的食物和住处，你们尽管享用。盛宴在三天后举行；我们只请求你们敞开心胸和头脑，来体验我们的生活方式。”马奎兹博士拄着手杖向前倾身，向你投来锐利的一瞥。“其实，我们是密斯卡托尼克大学派来做勘察的。”

• 在本战役余下的时间里，将1枚 [elder_thing] 标记加入混乱袋。

• 跳到 引言 4。

引言 4：蕾切尔嬷嬷听明白你的回答后，那副友善的面具只破了一瞬。“勘察者。我明白了。这里同样非常欢迎你们。但请守好你们的位置。我们有规矩。不要伤害山谷里的任何人，我们也不会伤害你们。夜里待在村子里，去荒野时要当心。这里的自然更残酷。”

沿路不远处，一只小母鹿与两个孩子并肩走着，仿佛在反驳这位女主人的话。你还没来得及多问她几句，一群本地人就涌向卡车，急着打听大陆上的消息。在回答了一连串关于体育赛事结果和选举的问题之后，马奎兹博士建议你们分头去结识当地人。“四处打听一下这座岛的事，一小时后回到这里碰头。”

specialRules.title: 在《铁杉谷盛宴》中游玩序曲

children.text:
• 本战役中的序曲要求调查员像游玩《诡镇奇谈：卡牌版》的传统关卡那样，设置地图、幕与议程牌库并进行游戏。

• 铁杉谷总体上是安全的地方。在这些序曲期间，没有遭遇牌库。这意味着调查员不能使用任何以任何方式与遭遇牌库互动的能力。（例如，搜寻遭遇牌库、从遭遇牌库抽牌或查看遭遇牌库中卡牌的效果都无法结算。）

• 了解居民们的所欲所求，以及他们白天都去往何处，是与他们每个人建立信任的关键。你与每位居民的关系会影响剧情，并会在之后的序曲中为你赢得奖励与经验。

• 铁杉谷是个囤积补给的好地方。序曲结束时，每位调查员保留以下内容：
• 手牌，最多保留至起始手牌数。（注意，调查员不会为 （第 [day] 日） 关卡进行传统的重调。）

• 游戏区中的资源，最多保留至起始资源数。

• 游戏区中一张通常不会在游戏开始时在场的支援卡。

• 其控制的所有线索。

• 有关序曲与关系等级的更多信息，请参阅本战役指南第2页的“附加规则与澄清”。

《铁杉谷盛宴》战役引入了一个全新的玩法概念：铁杉谷法典。在这场战役中，有些卡牌效果会指示玩家阅读特定的法典条目。游玩时请将战役指南放在手边，方便随时查阅。

《铁杉谷盛宴》中的某些地点、角色或敌人拥有法典条目，标记为（[codex] X）。要阅读某个角色或地点的法典条目，你必须先支付该能力上的所有费用，然后翻到本战役指南中当前关卡或序曲的法典部分，结算全部文本。

• 除非另有说明，每个法典条目在每场关卡或序曲中不能结算超过一次。

• 结算法典条目时，由触发该条目的玩家结算全部效果（进行检定、造成伤害、支付资源等）。如果无法确定是谁触发了该法典条目，则由队长结算该条目。

• 如果法典条目指示玩家将某位放在一边的具名居民加入游戏，除非另有说明，该角色以剧情支援面朝上加入游戏。

• 战役日志中名字已被划去的居民不能在序曲或关卡中进入游戏。如果某位居民的名字已被划去，该居民笔记中的全部条目也同样失效。

• 在为某个特定角色结算法典条目时，你只能阅读自己满足条件的单个小节。如果你不满足法典条目第一个小节的条件，就跳到下一个小节。除非另有说明，只参考该角色在你战役日志中的笔记与关系等级。（例如：“在瑞玟·霍桑的笔记中记录瑞玟是个万人迷”是指让玩家修改瑞玟战役日志条目中的“笔记”部分。）

• 结算完法典条目并在战役日志中做好变更后，恢复游戏。

《铁杉谷盛宴》战役只给玩家游戏内的三天时间来把整个故事走完。本战役还包含可游玩的序曲，调查员可以在其中与铁杉谷的居民互动、探寻铁杉岛的秘密，并为下一场关卡做准备。序曲是非对抗性的段落，会设置地点、剧本参考卡、幕与议程。每段序曲结束时都会给出若干选项，决定接下来游玩哪场关卡。视日期与时段而定，有些关卡会提供新的剧情选项或挑战。在一次战役的通关过程中，玩家没有时间游玩每一场关卡，也无法与每一位居民都交上朋友。

• 玩家在游玩序曲与幕间时可以赚取经验。把这些经验记录在“未花费经验”下，但在战役指南指示之前不要花费。

• 要掌握当前的日期／时段，你可以查看并更新战役日志中的“日期／时段”部分。

有时，剧情文本会指示调查员提高他们与某位特定居民的关系等级。若接到此类指示，请查看战役日志，找到该指定居民的条目。

• 提到某位居民的关系等级时，其条目中已勾选的格数就是该居民的关系等级。

• 要提高某位居民的关系等级，勾选该居民条目中最左侧未勾选的格子。

• 要降低某位居民的关系等级，擦掉该居民条目中最右侧已勾选的格子。

• 除非另有说明，每次只能提高或降低某位居民 1 格关系等级。

• 若接到将某位居民的关系等级设为 0 的指示，擦掉该居民条目中所有已勾选的格子。

• 战役日志中名字已被划去的居民不能在序曲或关卡中进入游戏。

本战役中的多数关卡按固定的网格样式摆放地点。在这些关卡中，每个地点除了连接图标之外，还与和它相邻的每个地点相连。

• 相邻的地点共享一条边（左边、右边、上方或下方）。只共享一个角的地点不算相邻。

• 接到将地点加入游戏的指示时，把它放在你所在地点上方、下方、左侧或右侧的相邻空位。

• 你不能把地点放到已有地点所在的位置上。选择新地点的位置时，若有可能，你必须选一个没有被地点占据的位置。若无法做到，则不将任何新地点加入游戏。

• 注意，在使用了“山谷”遭遇组的序曲与关卡中，地点只通过其图标相连。
本战役中的某些敌人拥有警戒关键词。每当调查员在尝试躲避拥有警戒关键词的敌人时技能检定失败，在结算完该次技能检定的所有结果之后，该敌人会对躲避它的调查员执行一次攻击。敌人在执行警戒攻击后不会横置。无论该敌人是否与躲避它的调查员交战，这次攻击都会发生。

在本战役中设置游戏时，玩家可能会被指示将时间标记卡加入游戏。为此，请从第一日、第二日或最终日遭遇组中找到与当前日期对应的时间标记卡，并将它放在议程牌库旁。这张卡代表当前的日期与时段。

有些卡牌会根据关卡发生在白日还是黑夜而产生不同效果。以（白日 [day]）或（黑夜 [night]）关键词开头的文本，只有所游玩的关卡或序曲分别处于白日或黑夜时才生效。前面没有这些关键词的任何其他能力，不论时段如何都生效。

设置指示可能会根据当前的日期与时段给出特定指示。（例如：“如果当前是第二日，将瑞玟·霍桑在蔓越莓沼泽加入游戏”这条指示只在把该关卡作为第二日关卡游玩时生效，在第二夜关卡中不生效。）

本战役中的某些敌人拥有逃逸关键词。逃逸敌人代表为了自保或达成自己的目标而想避开调查员的敌人。

如果处于重整状态且拥有逃逸关键词的敌人攻击或被攻击，在该次攻击结算之后，该敌人立即与所有调查员解除交战，移动到一个相连地点（若有可能，选择没有调查员的地点），然后横置。无论该敌人是否与攻击它的调查员交战，这个效果都会发生。

本战役中的某些敌人拥有巡逻关键词。在敌军阶段（框架步骤 3.2）中，每个处于重整状态且未交战、拥有巡逻关键词的敌人，会沿着通往指定地点（写在其巡逻字样旁的括号中）的最短路径移动到一个相连地点。

• 如果有多个地点都符合指定地点的条件，由队长选择该敌人向哪个地点移动。

• 如果拥有巡逻关键词的敌人会因卡牌能力阻挡的路径而被迫移动到一个地点，则该敌人不移动。

children.text:
[codex] 法典 1：蕾切尔嬷嬷

“星辰之子是什么人？”蕾切尔嬷嬷带着几分好笑，重复了你的问题。阳光穿透繁复的彩绘玻璃，在刺目的光柱中搅起浮尘。“如果非要我简单解释：我们都是。我常说，我们‘由光所生’。就像天体一样，我们每个人在此生都有一个位置、一个目的。有些人的位置是去理解。另一些人的位置则是去守望。”一排孩子鱼贯走入教堂，在祭坛旁盘腿坐下，这位年长的妇人淡淡一笑。“而现在，轮到我来开始讲故事了。”

你可以从手牌打出1张护符或法术支援，忽略其费用。

[codex] 法典 2：莉亚·阿特伍德

那位脸颊红润的年长妇人自我介绍说是莉亚·阿特伍德，蕾切尔嬷嬷的妹妹。“这一带的人吃进肚子里的所有东西，都归我管。没错，也就是说盛宴归我管。我姐姐对每一样要提前准备的东西都交代得格外仔细。”你向她打听铁杉岛上有哪些值得勘察的地方，她用戴着手套的手擦了擦额头。

“你几乎不用走出山谷，就能看见怪事，”她一手叉腰。“我今天打算上珍珠岭去。那上面的什么东西把树都变成了玻璃。我不确定那是不是你要找的，但那绝对独一无二。”

你可以从手牌打出1张工具卡，忽略其费用。

提高莉亚·阿特伍德的关系等级。

[codex] 法典 3：席米恩·阿特伍德

“小心，要炸了！”一个声音喊道，紧接着是一阵火花和鞭炮。一条白狗穿过烟雾朝你冲来，亲热地舔得你招架不住。一个胖乎乎、满脸雀斑的年轻人顶着一头鲜红的乱发跟了过来。

“啊，真是见鬼。我还以为你是希奥呢。别闹了，迪格比！”他对狗说，然后单膝跪下收拾残局。“抱歉。我叫席米恩。我妈总是忙着给蕾切尔姨妈做饭，”他挠了挠脖子上那块红色、隆起的硬化皮肤。“蕾切尔姨妈说，要是在山谷里乱丢东西，我们就要挨5鞭子。”你向他打听岛上有哪些值得一看的地方。“珍珠岭上面的矿场不许去。那是我为我的秘密社团占下的，”这个年轻人说。

从你的牌库顶9张牌中搜寻1张战术或诡计卡，将其加入手牌（洗牌）。

提高席米恩·阿特伍德的关系等级。

[codex] 法典 4：威廉·汉洛克

在山谷学校外，你向一位男子致意，他自我介绍说是威廉·汉洛克。“我听说有访客来了。只是没想到这么快就见到你们。没错，我就是汉洛克家族最后的在世继承人，”他没等你发问便夸口道。“不过，要是那个不请自来的瑞玟得逞，也许我就不是最后的了，”他咬牙切齿地说。你注意到他腋下夹着一本翻旧的《瓦尔登湖》，便向他打听当地有哪些值得一看的地方。“我知道这有点不合常理，但我家老宅里有一处……古怪的虫害，”他似乎把话在嘴里嚼了一遍。“如果你能把那东西除掉，而不是研究它，我想我们大家都会感激你。”

从你的牌库顶9张牌中搜寻1张典籍或天赋卡，将其加入手牌（洗牌）。

提高威廉·汉洛克的关系等级。

[codex] 法典 5：瑞玟·霍桑

“我跟‘伟大的侧影’是朋友。你可能知道他的本名，约翰·巴里摩尔。我们是在罗马的一座广场上认识的。纯属机缘巧合。”瑞玟一边和伯蒂聊天，一边兴致勃勃地说。“虽然我姓霍桑，但你要知道，我可是地地道道的汉洛克家的人。汉洛克家产的最后一位继承人。前提是亲爱的威廉真肯听人说话，”他们酸溜溜地说。伯蒂又招架了好几个关于纽约上流社会近况的问题——而他对这些一无所知——随后才向瑞玟打听值得一去的地方。“我听说北岬矿井里有些迷人的水晶，”他们答道。

这对表亲坐在海岸边，隔着堤道眺望大陆。海鸥在灰暗起伏的浪面上低飞。“铁杉岛本来会是个很糟的避风头的地方。我在纽约的朋友们已经在私下议论我的失势了，”瑞玟苦涩地说。威廉端详着自己的表亲。“我想我该回到社交界去了。我肯定能把你朋友们的看法纠正过来。”瑞玟顿了顿，随即想到一个主意，露出坏笑。“哦，威廉。我的朋友们会喜欢你的。你只要分享一首你写的诗就行。我保证他们会觉得那首诗迷人极了。”

[codex] 法典 7：朱迪斯·帕克

朱迪斯朝你走来，猎装上溅满血迹，头发乱糟糟的，步枪斜挎在肩上。看到你担忧的神情，她低头看了看自己的外套。“哦，别担心。你该看看另一个人成了什么样，”她眨眨眼。你问她是否还打算去波士顿，她耸了耸肩。“也许吧，也许不去了。我正想问你接下来要去哪儿。”

你告诉她你要去阿卡姆，她憋住了一声不信的嗤笑。“阿卡姆，是吗？那个每隔一周就因为怪事上新闻的城市？你真要回那儿去？”她沉默了片刻，像是在考虑什么。“你会需要有人替你看着后背，”她试探着说。你告诉她你打算好好休息一阵，她咧嘴一笑。“我有个朋友在东城的某个地方开了家地下酒馆。经历了这么多事，我看我欠你一杯酒。”

[codex] 法典 8：希奥·彼得斯

你走近时，希奥不好意思地笑了，然后给了你一个熊抱。他松开手时，你发现他在哭。你问他为什么，他低下头。“我真的不知道为什么。”他停下来想了想，又继续说。“我一直想要一个……一个重新有家的感觉的地方。爸妈走了以后，海伦变得——她变得很难相处。后来我开始在山谷里帮忙，而他们不在乎我有多难缠。那里感觉像家。现在那也没了。”他眨了眨眼，眨去泪水。“我想家是自己造出来的吧。你什么时候该来波特兰看看我们。我知道你会喜欢的，”他笑了。

尾声 1：1926年6月

致亨利·阿米蒂奇博士办公室：

铁杉岛的勘察已经结束，而马奎兹博士没能回来。我们在那座荒凉岛屿上的所见所闻，完全无法用常理解释。一种异类的存在支配着当地的生态系统，扭曲了附近每一个生物的身心健康。我们见证了一些从未被记录过的物种，而且今后很可能再也无法记录。当地人与此存在共存了数十年，表面上——或者刻意地——对其退化性的影响毫不知情。有些人甚至崇拜它。我们自认能活下来已是万幸。

不幸的是，马奎兹博士没有这样的运气。随信附上一份详尽的报告，记录了她对这片独特生态系统的观察。报告里没有写到的，是她如何——以及何等英勇地——献出了自己的生命。那个故事，我们希望能当面讲给你听。出于对她遗志的敬意，我们请求你不要把这些记录当作纯粹的臆想而不予理会。谨上，

密斯卡托尼克勘察队

Intro 1: June 1926

Miskatonic Survey, June 1926. Members Marquez, Musgrave, et alii.

After three separate reviews by Miskatonic University’s board and grant commitee, we have reached Hemlock Isle. Our driver took us across a natural land-bridge they call the “causeway”—only traversible at low tide—to a small fishing village called Akwan. Bertie showed the locals several sketches and photographs of the alkaline blossom, but the locals would have none of it. Or maybe none of him. Bertie is exceedingly chipper.

The survey consists of myself, my assistant Bertie Musgrave, and some contacts of Dr. Armitage. He insisted they accompany me as part of the terms of the grant. I just hope they don’t get in the way. The island is private property and has been off-limits to visitors for some time—until now. The locals are advertising some kind of festival throughout New England, even as far south as Boston and Arkham.

There were no lodgings in Akwan, and according to local rumors, camping on the island is a risky affair. The locals were unresponsive when I pressed further, but I was at least able to procure a map of the island as well as some basic supplies. We were all but resigned to pitching a tent west of Akwan, but then we met a young man named Theo who offered us lodging in a village called ‘Hemlock Vale’.

Dr. Rosa Marquez

“But really, I think you’re gonna love it here,” Theo shouts from the truck window. Dr. Marquez—athletic and well-tanned at 40—closes her survey journal and looks up at the sky. “I don’t know anyone who doesn’t love Hemlock Isle,” Theo continues. “And I don’t know why we haven’t invited folks sooner! I assume you’re here for the Feast.”

“Is this feast some sort of local tradition?” Bertie says in a crisp British accent. The breeze stirs the round man’s shock of thick hair as he leans forward eagerly.

“This is the first one ever! Everyone in the Vale’s pulled out all the stops so everyone feels welcome. We’re just so excited to have visitors!” The young man laughs as your truck crests the hilltop. Hemlock Isle stretches away in every direction.

To the south, glistening black lakes dot a tangled marsh all the way to the coast. Up north, whitecapped hills gather around jutting obsidian rocks, resembling an exposed spine. Past a huddle of hills, the dense western forest grows up the rocky hillside, bisected by a wide river. And even further north, past the white hills, is a bleak rocky coastline at the edge of the slatey Atlantic waters.

The road takes you past lush farmland into a village nestled in the hills. Gaudy floral arrangments and brilliant ribbons hang from rooftops and fenceposts. A prismatic rainbow shimmers in a cloudless sky, lending the scene an idyllic air. As the truck rolls to a stop in the crossroads, locals and children in white-gold cloaks and wooden animal masks gather around you, grinning from ear to ear.

“Willkommen!” An imposing woman with steel-gray hair and a white-gold cloak cuts through the crowd. “Welcome to Hemlock Vale. I am Mother Rachel, and these are my people. What brings you here?”

Down the road, a small doe walks alongside a pair of children, almost as if to contradict the matron’s words. Before you can ask her more, a gaggle of locals descend on the truck, eager for news from the mainland. After fielding multiple questions about sports outcomes and elections, Dr. Marquez suggests you split up to acquaint yourselves with the locals. “Ask around about the island and meet back here in an hour.”

specialRules.title: Playing Preludes in The Feast of Hemlock Vale

children.text:
• Preludes in this campaign require investigators to set up a map, act and agenda deck and play much like they would a traditional scenario of Arkham Horror: The Card Game.

• Hemlock Vale is generally a safe place. During these preludes, there is no encounter deck. This means that the investigators cannot use abilities that interact with the encounter deck in any way. (For example, effects such as those that search the encounter deck, draw cards from the encounter deck, or look at cards in the encounter deck cannot be resolved.)

• Understanding the residents’ wants and needs, as well as where they go during the day, is key to building trust with each of them. Your relationship with each resident influences the story and will earn you rewards and experience in later preludes.

• Hemlock Vale is a good place to stock up on supplies. At the end of a prelude, each investigator keeps the following:
• Cards in hand, up to their opening hand size. (Note that investigators do not take a traditional mulligan for (Day [day]) scenarios.)

• Resources in play, up to their starting resources.

• A single asset in their play area that does not normally start in play.

• All clues they control.

• For more information on Preludes and Relationship Levels, refer to the Additional Rules and Clarifications on page 2 of this Campaign Guide.

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign features a new gameplay concept: The Codex. During this campaign, some card effects may direct players to read a specific codex entry. While playing, keep the Campaign Guide on hand for easy reference.

Certain locations, characters, or enemies in The Feast of Hemlock Vale have codex entries, marked with ([codex] X). To read a character or location’s codex entry, you must pay all costs on that ability first, then turn to the current scenario or prelude’s Codex in this Campaign Guide and resolve all text.

• Each codex entry cannot be resolved more than once per scenario or prelude unless otherwise stated.

• When resolving a codex entry, the player who triggered that entry resolves all effects (resolving a test, dealing damage, paying resources, etc.). If it is unclear who triggered the codex entry, the lead investigator resolves the entry.

• If a codex entry instructs players to put a named set-aside resident into play, put that character into play with their story asset side faceup unless otherwise stated.

• A resident whose name is crossed out in your Campaign Log cannot enter play during preludes or scenarios. If a resident’s name is crossed out, so are all entries in that resident’s Notes.

• While resolving a codex entry for a specific character, you may only read a single section for which you meet the requirements. If you do not meet the requirements for the first section of a codex entry, skip to the following section. Only refer to that character’s Notes and Relationship Level in your Campaign Log unless otherwise stated. (e.g. “In River Hawthorne’s Notes, record River is a dreamboat” directs players to change the “Notes” section in River’s Campaign Log entry.)

• After resolving a codex entry and making any changes in your Campaign Log, resume play.

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign gives players just three days in-game to play out its story. This campaign also contains playable preludes in which investigators may interact with the residents of Hemlock Vale, learn the secrets of Hemlock Isle, and make preparations for the next scenario. Preludes are non-confrontational segments that are set up with locations and a scenario reference, act, and agenda. The end of each prelude provides several choices on which scenario to play next. Depending on the day and time, some scenarios may provide new story options or challenges. Players will not have time to play every scenario or befriend each resident on a single playthrough of this campaign.

• Players may earn experience when playing preludes and interludes. Record this experience under “Unspent Experience,” but do not spend it until instructed to by the campaign guide.

• To keep track of the current day/time, you may refer to and update the “Day/Time” section in the Campaign Log.

At times, story text may instruct investigators to increase their Relationship Level with a particular resident. If instructed to do so, check the Campaign Log and find the specified resident’s entry.

• When referring to a resident’s Relationship Level, the number of checked boxes in their entry is that resident’s Relationship Level.

• To increase a resident’s Relationship Level, check the leftmost unchecked box in that resident’s entry.

• To decrease a resident’s Relationship Level, erase the rightmost checked box in that resident’s entry.

• Unless otherwise stated, you should increase or decrease a resident’s Relationship Level by 1 box at a time.

• If instructed to set a resident’s Relationship Level to 0, erase all checked boxes in that resident’s entry.

• A resident whose name is crossed out in your Campaign Log cannot enter play during preludes or scenarios.

Most scenarios in this campaign are arranged in a set grid pattern. During these scenarios, each location is connected to each location adjacent to it, in addition to any connection icons.

• Adjacent locations share a side (left, right, above, or below). Locations that share only a corner are not considered adjacent.

• When instructed to put a location into play, place it in an adjacent empty space above, below, or to the left or right of your location.

• You cannot put a location into play where an existing location already is. When choosing where to put a new location, you must choose a spot unoccupied by a location, if able. If you cannot, no new locations are put into play.

• Note that during preludes and scenarios that utilize The Vale encounter set, locations are only connected via their icons.

Some enemies in this campaign have the alert keyword. Each time an investigator fails a skill test while attempting to evade an enemy with the alert keyword, after applying all results for that skill test, that enemy performs an attack against the evading investigator. An enemy does not exhaust after performing an alert attack. This attack occurs whether the enemy is engaged with the evading investigator or not.

During setup during this campaign, players may be instructed to put the Time Marker card into play. To do so, find the Time Marker card in the The First Day, The Second Day, or The Final Day encounter sets that corresponds to the current day and place it next to the agenda deck. This is the current day and time.

Some cards have different effects depending on whether the scenario takes place during the Day or Night. Text following a (Day [day]) or (Night [night]) keyword is only active if the scenario or prelude being played is during the Day or Night, respectively. Any other ability not preceded by these keywords is active regardless of the time period.

Setup instructions may have specific instructions depending on the current day and time. (e.g. “If it is Day 2, put River Hawthorne into play at the Cranberry Bog” only applies when playing that scenario as a Day 2 scenario and not a Night 2 scenario).

Some enemies in this campaign have the elusive keyword. Elusive enemies represent enemies who want to avoid the investigators for their own survival or to accomplish their own goals.

If a ready enemy with the elusive keyword attacks or is attacked, after that attack resolves, that enemy immediately disengages from all investigators, moves to a connecting location (with no investigators, if able), and exhausts. This effect occurs whether the enemy was engaged with the attacking investigator or not.

Some enemies in this campaign have the patrol keyword. During the enemy phase (in framework step 3.2), each ready, unengaged enemy with the patrol keyword moves to a connecting location along the shortest path toward the designated location (as described in parentheses next to the word patrol).

• If there are multiple locations that qualify as the designated location, the lead investigator may choose which location the enemy moves toward.

• If an enemy with patrol would be compelled to move to a location via a path that is blocked by a card ability, the enemy does not move.

[codex] Codex 1: Mother Rachel

“What are the Children of the Stars?” Mother Rachel echoes your question, bemused. Dust swirls in the harsh light through the intricate stained glass. “I suppose if I had to put it simply: We all are. ‘Begotten by light,’ I often say. Like heavenly bodies, we each have a place in this life, a purpose. There are some whose place is to understand. And others whose place is to watch.” The older woman smiles faintly as a line of children file into the chapel to sit cross-legged near the altar. “And now, it is my place to begin storytime.”

You may play a Charm or Spell asset from your hand, ignoring its cost.

[codex] Codex 2: Leah Atwood

The red-cheeked older woman introduces herself as Leah Atwood, Mother Rachel’s sister. “I’m in charge of everything folks around here put in their bellies. And yes, that means I’m in charge of the Feast. My sister has been very particular about everything she wants prepared in advance.” You ask her about any points of interest to survey in Hemlock Isle, and she wipes her brow with a gloved hand.

“You barely need to leave the Vale before you see something odd,” she puts one hand on her hip. “I’m planning to go up to Pearl Ridge today. Something up there turned the trees to glass. I’m not sure if that’s what you’re looking for, but it is definitely unique.”

[codex] Codex 3: Simeon Atwood

“Fire in the hole!” shouts a voice, followed by a shower of sparks and firecrackers. A white dog barrels through the smoke toward you, and you are assailed with friendly licks. A chubby freckled young man with a shock of bright red hair follows.

“Ah, marbles. I thought you were Theo. Lay off, Digby!” he tells the dog, then drops to one knee to gather the debris. “Sorry about that. I’m Simeon. My ma’s always busy cooking for Auntie Rachel,” he scratches a red, raised swirl of hardened skin on his neck. “Auntie Rachel said we’d get 5 lashes if we litter in the Vale.” You ask him about any points of interest on the island. “You’re not allowed to go to the mines up in Pearl Ridge. I claimed them for my secret society,” the young man says.

[codex] Codex 4: William Hemlock

Outside the Vale schoolhouse, you greet a man who introduces himself as William Hemlock. “I’d heard we had visitors. I just didn’t expect to meet them so soon. And yes, I am the last living heir to the Hemlock Family,” he blusters, although you didn’t ask. “Or perhaps not the very last, if that gatecrasher River has their way,” he snarls. You note the worn copy of Walden under his arm, and ask about any local points of interest. “I know it’s rather unconventional, but my family’s old house has a…peculiar infestation,” he seems to chew his own words. “If you could exterminate whatever it is rather than study it, I think we’d all be in your debt.”

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign features a new gameplay concept: The Codex. During this campaign, some card effects may direct players to read a specific codex entry. While playing, keep the Campaign Guide on hand for easy reference.

Certain locations, characters, or enemies in The Feast of Hemlock Vale have codex entries, marked with ([codex] X). To read a character or location’s codex entry, you must pay all costs on that ability first, then turn to the current scenario or prelude’s Codex in this Campaign Guide and resolve all text.

• Each codex entry cannot be resolved more than once per scenario or prelude unless otherwise stated.

• When resolving a codex entry, the player who triggered that entry resolves all effects (resolving a test, dealing damage, paying resources, etc.). If it is unclear who triggered the codex entry, the lead investigator resolves the entry.

• If a codex entry instructs players to put a named set-aside resident into play, put that character into play with their story asset side faceup unless otherwise stated.

If you do not meet the requirements for the first section of a codex entry, skip to the folowing section. Only refer to that character’s Notes and Relationship Level in your Campaign Log unless otherwise stated. • After resolving a codex entry and making any changes in your Campaign Log, resume play.

Three Days, Three Nights

The Feast of Hemlock Vale campaign gives players just three days in-game to play out its story. This campaign also contains playable preludes in which investigators may interact with the residents of Hemlock Vale, learn the secrets of Hemlock Isle, and make preparations for the next scenario.

Preludes are non-confrontational segments that are set up with locations and a scenario reference, act, and agenda. The end of each prelude provides several choices on which scenario to play next. Depending on the day and time, some scenarios may provide new story options or challenges. Players will not have time to play every scenario or befriend each resident on a single playthrough of this campaign.

• Players may earn experience when playing preludes and interludes. Record this experience under “Unspent Experience,” but do not spend it until instructed to by the campaign guide.

• To keep track of the current day/time, you may refer to and update the “Day/Time” section in the Campaign Log.

Residents & Relationship Levels

At times, story text may instruct investigators to increase their Relationship Level with a particular resident. If instructed to do so, check the Campaign Log and find the specified resident’s entry.

• When referring to a resident’s Relationship Level, the number of checked boxes in their entry is that resident’s Relationship Level.

• To increase a resident’s Relationship Level, check the leftmost unchecked box in that resident’s entry.

• To decrease a resident’s Relationship Level, erase the rightmost checked box in that resident’s entry.

• Unless otherwise stated, you should increase or decrease a resident’s Relationship Level by 1 box at a time.

• If instructed to set a resident’s Relationship Level to 0, erase all checked boxes in that resident’s entry.

• A resident whose name is crossed out in your Campaign Log cannot enter play during preludes or scenarios.

Location Adjacency in this Campaign

Most scenarios in this campaign are arranged in a set grid pattern. During these scenarios, each location is connected to each location adjacent to it, in addition to any connection icons.

• Adjacent locations share a side (left, right, above, or below). Locations that share only a corner are not considered adjacent.

• When instructed to put a location into play, place it in an adjacent empty space above, below, or to the left or right of your location.

• You cannot put a location into play where an existing location already is. When choosing where to put a new location, you must choose a spot unoccupied by a location, if able. If you cannot, no new locations are put into play.

• Note that during preludes and scenarios that utilize The Vale encounter set, locations are only connected via their icons.

Alert

Some enemies in this campaign have the alert keyword. Each time an investigator fails a skill test while attempting to evade an enemy with the alert keyword, after applying all results for that skill test, that enemy performs an attack against the evading investigator. An enemy does not exhaust after performing an alert attack. This attack occurs whether the enemy is engaged with the evading investigator or not.

Day [day] and Night [night]

During setup during this campaign, players may be instructed to put the Time Marker card into play. To do so, find the Time Marker card in the The First Day, The Second Day, or The Final Day encounter sets that corresponds to the current day and place it next to the agenda deck. This is the current day and time.

Some cards have different effects depending on whether the scenario takes place during the Day or Night. Text following a (Day [day]) or (Night [night]) keyword is only active if the scenario or prelude being played is during the Day or Night, respectively. Any other ability not preceded by these keywords is active regardless of the time period.

Setup instructions may have specific instructions depending on the current day and time. (e.g. “If it is Day 2, put River Hawthorne into play at the Cranberry Bog” only applies when playing that scenario as a Day 2 scenario and not a Night 2 scenario).

Elusive

Some enemies in this campaign have the elusive keyword. Elusive enemies represent enemies who want to avoid the investigators for their own survival or to accomplish their own goals.

If a ready enemy with the elusive keyword attacks or is attacked, after that attack resolves, that enemy immediately disengages from all investigators, moves to a connecting location (with no investigators, if able), and exhausts. This effect occurs whether the enemy was engaged with the attacking investigator or not.

Patrol

Some enemies in this campaign have the patrol keyword. During the enemy phase (in framework step 3.2), each ready, unengaged enemy with the patrol keyword moves to a connecting location along the shortest path toward the designated location (as described in parentheses next to the word patrol).

• If there are multiple locations that qualify as the designated location, the lead investigator may choose which location the enemy moves toward.

• If an enemy with patrol would be compelled to move to a location via a path that is blocked by a card ability, the enemy does not move.
